The two towers on the horizon symbolize the final material obstacles. They seem threatening only until we have left the misleading moonlight behind, in order to tread the illuminated path.

At this stage of their journey, initiates must once again gather all their courage and knowledge, if they do not wish to be distracted by various outer circumstances. In the Tarot of the Aquarian Age, the moon completely covers the sun. The moon has no light of its own, which means it reflects the sunlight. It appears to shine, but this apparent brightness is illusory, a deception. Although it charms both man and woman, we must learn to see through this charm.

The Moon is the card of dreams that rise out of the sea of the unconscious. As a mystical card, the Moon leads us into another reality. The path leading through the towers parts ways with the earthly dimension and plunges into the sphere of an otherworldly reality.

The Hebrew letter depicted on card number eighteen is QOPH (eye of the needle). It is also the human path leading from the world of commerce, from the here and now, through the gate of the invisible into the world of the future that lies beyond.

The rune of the card is OTHALA, meaning the land of Odal. OTHALA is the sacred boundary. Within it is contained the fundamental plan and the idea of "inner" and "outer." It signifies a place that has been set apart to serve sacred purposes, a temple or a center of worship. OTHALA describes the essence of the tidal mysteries of ebb and flow, which, as is well known, are governed by the Moon.

The Moon is the card of the "wanderer between two worlds." These wanderers are close to overcoming the last fear associated with physical incarnation, so that they may fully immerse themselves in the world of the sun.

title: The Sun
description:
"Self-realization is the source of all knowledge."
Lu Chu Yuan

After the stars and the moonlight, sunlight finally appears in the Tarot. The half-lit, hazy uncertainty surrounding the Moon disappears, and with it goes every trace of the insecurity and ignorance that has accompanied the young Magician from the first card all the way to the card of the Moon. The great Sun, granting clarity, allows everything to shine with new light.

Although the word is feminine in gender, in German and in many other languages the Sun is considered exclusively masculine. It is called "the Lord of Light" or "the Lord of Life," because without the sun life would be impossible. It is also known as "the Lord of Love," because it gives us light and warmth freely, asking nothing in return. In the end, the Sun is also "the Lord of Freedom," because without our own inner suns, we could not experience boundless freedom.

In the background of the Tarot of the Aquarian Age card, we see a human figure standing atop a mountain, raising its arms in the joy of life and freedom. This person is free as a bird. He looks as though he wishes for nothing more than to fly to the Sun, to express gratitude for all the good that has been bestowed upon him. Throughout the whole of his life, the Sun has always given him nourishment and joy.

Life pours forth from the solar disk on the Tarot card, as a sign of the rebirth of the eternal bond between heaven and earth. Life is sustained by life.

In the foreground we see a sketch. On the right is depicted a brick wall, and two halves of a sunflower above it. One of these flowers has been fully drawn, the other is merely a sketch. The wall represents a protective wall, behind which people who have reached the phase of development shown on this card find refuge, shielding their happiness, joy and success from hostile eyes. The sunflowers behind this wall symbolize the fact that the initiate has rediscovered harmony with nature. The unfinished sunflower represents the initiate's vow to respect and protect nature, so that future generations may find life on Earth worth living.

The card of the Sun signifies total realization on the plane of matter, soul and mind. This is the card of harmony, of happiness with your partner and in your profession. It embodies ideas such as self-confidence, self-knowledge, awareness and independence. The man and woman who have developed thus far along the path of the Tarot can, at last, enjoy the fruits of their success. Deep love and humility characterize such individuals, since they have learned that everything that comes into their life is, in truth, a gift from God. But this card also embodies the liberation of the sexes: there is no longer a state of polarity, the masculine and the feminine are in harmony. The opposites have merged. This does not mean that man and woman will no longer make sexual love. On the contrary, they truly will: each will love the other in awareness of his or her individuality and with respect for the other, for the Thou. In this most intimate act of love, both can understand that the power that moves them to love was, is, and always will be the energy of God. The woman embodies the feminine source of this aspect, receiving and giving shelter; the man embodies the masculine source, which creates and protects. Together, man and woman once again form a unity, and their eternal longing is finally satisfied.

From the standpoint of numerology, the card of the Sun bears the number nineteen, a very mystical number. The sum of its digits equals ten. The first digit in the number ten (one) symbolizes unity; the second digit (zero) symbolizes infinite space. Ten is thus the fulfillment and completion of creation.

The Hebrew letter of the card is RESH (head). Just as the head directs the body, so too will positive qualities eventually outweigh the negative. Humanity will be able to pass through the "eye of the needle," represented by the letter QOPH on the previous card. Filled with joy and excitement, the heavens await humanity.

The rune GEBO means gift. GEBO embodies generosity and hospitality toward guests. Generous people are those who can allow things to happen. By giving freely, they open the gates through which abundance and joy can enter their lives. GEBO also symbolizes the mystery of sexual union and the transcendence of polarities.

The astrological sign of the card is the Sun, the source of vital energy. The power of the Sun awakens the passive soul, wandering lost in the earthly. The Sun rules whenever life energies rise, when the will to act comes to the fore. The Sun awakens human beings from lethargy and accompanies them to the next phase, or card, where the awakened and the initiated await us.

title: Judgement
description:
"Should I reveal the great secret to you, my friend? Do not wait for the Day of Judgement: it happens every day."
Albert Camus

The Judgement that the spiritual seeker encounters here is not a strict and punishing judgment, but rather a liberating state of rebirth. Through the influence of the Sun, alchemical transformation has so ennobled and purified the human body that the rebirth of the spirit can take place. In order to attain mastery, the initiate must walk the path of death and resurrection several times, growing purer and more transparent each time.

The card of Judgement embodies the state of resurrection that follows the death of initiation. The man and woman who live because of their deaths know that every awakening means more than simply serving them personally. Since every individual is a representative of a family, a group or a race, everything an individual understands or teaches also serves other people. In this light, the spiritual path is neither lonely nor long, but instead carries us toward the greatest awareness of responsibility for ourselves and others. People who have reached this stage no longer belong to any dogmatic, esoteric religion, but live within themselves the unity of all religions — a genuine universal religion.

Card number twenty in the Tarot of the Aquarian Age depicts a remarkably beautiful young woman, whose wide-open, knowing eyes gaze lovingly upon everything she sees. When we compare this card with the card of the High Priestess, we recognize that the same young woman is depicted on both cards. On the second card, her eyes are closed; on the twentieth card, her eyes are fully open. She has awakened, having revealed her mystery, and now she helps awaken others, blowing loudly on her trumpet. She is like the Archangel Gabriel, who awakens people from an enchanted spell, from their long sleep, into a new state of consciousness.

On the left side of the card is shown the process of Judgement, as drawn by Pamela Colman Smith in her Tarot deck. Seven notes issue from the trumpet blown by the angels. Beneath the trumpet we see a young woman on the right, a man on the left, and a boy between them. All three are naked, their nakedness symbolizing that they have risen from the graves of their limited consciousness. Nakedness in the Tarot invariably signifies consciousness. The graves signify that the bodily aspect has been left far behind. The male figure on the right represents tradition: all the philosophical, religious, intellectual and artistic paths of the past, as well as the masculine side of each of us. The female figure represents feeling, the heart, worshipful love and intuition, as well as the feminine side of each of us. The youth in the middle combines the aspects of father and mother within himself, and is thus ready for mastery and prepared for full awakening.

This twentieth card also has a bearing on our present day and age: our twentieth century literally proclaims awakening aloud. A collective, spiritual awakening into higher consciousness and toward a more responsible attitude to the environment and our fellow human beings, regardless of differences in skin color or race, is the one true mission worth every individual's effort.

SHIN (tooth) is the Hebrew letter belonging to card number twenty. If people had no teeth, they would not be able to eat, and would be doomed to die. Similarly, human destiny is also divided into small parts; thus time was born: hours, years and centuries. Everything completes itself according to the great cosmic plan. Time unfolds within the spiritual life of humanity. Only God knows everything — the beginning and the end.

The rune PERTHRO (dice-cup) is assigned to card number twenty. As the rune of fate, PERTHRO symbolizes the weaving of the three Fates of Norse or Germanic mythology, who represent past, present and future. In reality, all fate takes place simultaneously within the realm of the runes.

The astrological sign of this card is dedicated to Pluto, god of the Underworld. Pluto rules the realm of the dead, and is thus closely connected with death and transformation. The path of the Tarot now leads the initiate to the highest stage of completion, embodied by the next card, the World.

title: The World
description:
"No two are alike; yet all are alike before the Almighty. How can this be? Because each is perfect in itself."
Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

The path of the Tarot is nearing its end. The seeker has arrived at the solution to the mystery, liberation from this World. Or is it liberation into this World? Regardless of the plane on which the outcome unfolds, initiates have completed their process of initiation. Now, at the end of their long journey, they understand: the path never existed, and they have always been here.

Carlos Castaneda defined the world as "a separate reality." As long as seekers on the path perceive the world as something separate, they remain on that path. But as the veil falls from their eyes and they behold the truth of their spirit, every cell of their body instantly understands that separation never existed, and could never have existed. The seeker has always been and remains everything: mountains, rivers, trees, shrubs, animals, flying birds, even the tiny ants crawling around the seeker's feet. The wanderer is identical with all creation.

This understanding is granted to the initiate in a moment of bliss, called illumination. This sensation is so profound, so deeply shocking, that it can never be forgotten again. If the initiate is everything and has always been everything, then it becomes obvious that everything external is also part of the initiate. Alienation, the sense of separateness that caused such intense pain, disappears, and the wanderers find themselves in the midst of unity. If an ever-greater number of people were to live on earth with this incomparable experience, love and understanding would reign throughout the whole earth, since all people would recognize their own part existing within every other person. Intolerance, envy and aggression, being expressions of ignorance, would simply gradually disappear. People who know will no longer feel this way. Love, tolerance and understanding for every living creature will find a place in their hearts. Every individual will belong to the great "I AM."

The World is like a carousel, an eternal dance. Nothing stands still, because motion is the engine of the material world, and life arises from this motion. If you remain at the stage of "not knowing," you can still lose yourself in the dance and the whirl of the world. But if you have become "one who knows," you have reached the middle of the spinning world and sense eternal life.

A very expressive image on card number twenty-one depicts a woman in the midst of an infinite Universe. A serpent is coiled around her, but she no longer fears this creature and its power. Instead, she even strokes it gently, and the tamed creature bows its head in a sign of devotion and worship. Many chains surround the woman, but all of them have been broken. This shows that the woman is free of every fetter and every debt, her karma resolved, and she works willingly to help liberate the World. Her eyes are closed, but she can nonetheless feel the whole World with all its joys and its pain. She is the liberated Eve, the truth that shows itself without a veil. Behind the veil, the secret essence of all being reveals itself. To know this secret is to master universal freedom and to gain the power that results from that freedom. All of this is bestowed by perfect initiation. Admitted to the streams of divine light, human beings have risen out of their fallen state, become one with the light, and leave the Wheel of Rebirth.

The World carries out the divine plan. The heavens open their gates and bestow upon us the gift of understanding the meaning of the eternal cycle of coming into and departing from existence. Everyone strives to find their fulfillment in active participation in the great process of life.

TAV (mark, sign) is the last letter of the Hebrew alphabet. It embodies the "sign" in the sense of a blessing — the Divine blessing upon the completion of the task.

The rune of card number twenty-one is another form of the rune GEBO which, as we saw in connection with card number nineteen, means "gift." In this card, GEBO embodies success and constructive cooperation.

Saturn is the astrological sign of this card. Saturn is the sign of limitation, slowing and restraint. But transcended Saturn signifies the end of all limitation, fetters and bonds.

The card of the World is the card of fullness, the end of the path. It is the card of the consciousness of the individual, of the divine soul in harmony with the absolute SPIRIT.

title: Ace of Wands
description: The Ace of Wands is a pure, primal beginning: a spark of creative fire, the courage to take the first step, and the resolve to carry an intention through into action. This card speaks of new energy ready to be brought to life, if you find the courage to accept it.

title: Two of Wands
description: The Two of Wands is creative energy already gathered, still waiting to be directed into the right channel. This card is about mastering your own will and taking a situation firmly in hand, so the force behind it isn't allowed to scatter and go to waste.

title: Three of Wands
description: The Three of Wands says that directed energy leads to success when it is backed by virtue, honesty, and self-confidence. This is a card of progress built on a solid inner foundation, not on chance luck.

title: Four of Wands
description: The Four of Wands is the completion of an important stage, success made secure through independent creative work. This card marks the moment when your efforts begin to bear fruit, and invites you to consolidate what has been achieved before moving on.

title: Five of Wands
description: The Five of Wands is a challenge and a test of your own strength: the situation calls for a readiness to stand up to difficulty and not back down. This card reminds you that beneath the tension of competition lies a drive toward harmony and eventual success.

title: Six of Wands
description: The Six of Wands brings success, recognition, and a victory won through your own strength and sound decisions. This is a card of well-earned triumph: consistent, considered conduct guarantees that fortune stays on your side.

title: Seven of Wands
description: The Seven of Wands speaks of overcoming resistance — things around you may feel crowded and tense, but courage, boldness, and a willingness to take risks will be rewarded. This card is about staying steady at the moment when it would be easier to give up.

title: Eight of Wands
description: The Eight of Wands promises a swift resolution and good news arriving sooner than you expect. Truth dispels misunderstanding, and obstacles that only recently seemed impossible to overcome finally clear from your path.

title: Nine of Wands
description: The Nine of Wands is resistance to new experience and energy accumulated over a long time that now needs careful, right application. This card reminds you that the strength you have been storing must be used wisely, not squandered.

title: Ten of Wands
description: The Ten of Wands speaks of being weighed down and oppressed — energy held back, strength smothered under the load of too many obligations. This card warns: if you try to carry everything at once, sooner or later you will have to stop and rethink the burden.

title: Princess of Wands
description: The Princess of Wands is simplicity, femininity, and a fiery, impulsive energy full of passion and optimism. She carries a magnetic, captivating pull and a moody changeability of temper: capable of a brief but brilliant response to whatever genuinely ignites her, and keenly attuned to both anxiety and desire.

title: Prince of Wands
description: The Prince of Wands is a young, dynamic, fiery energy full of tension and passion. His is a hot, slightly reckless young love and a chivalrous impulse that can lack attentiveness: he is easily carried away, acting out of a self-centered but sincere delight.

title: Queen of Wands
description: The Queen of Wands is a mature femininity and a fiery energy backed by will and steadfastness. She knows how to stand up for herself while keeping her warmth, depth, and a genuine capacity to feel and give love.

title: Knight of Wands
description: The Knight of Wands is a mature masculinity and a fiery, self-assured energy. He devotes himself to an idea and a mission, acts with drive and directness, and knows how to stand up for himself and for those dear to him — a fierce, dependable protector.

title: Ace of Cups
description: The Ace of Cups is the deepest fulfillment and love in all its forms. This card offers the great opportunity to find yourself through an open heart, and reminds you that the wellspring of real joy is already overflowing and ready to pour into your life.

title: Two of Cups
description: The Two of Cups is a meeting with love and the birth of a harmonious, mutual relationship. This card speaks of a reciprocity of feeling, when two hearts find each other and begin to flow in the same rhythm.

title: Three of Cups
description: The Three of Cups is abundance, joy, and fullness that make you want to genuinely thank life. This card is about moments of real happiness shared with those close to you, and the feeling that the cup of your life is full right now.

title: Four of Cups
description: The Four of Cups warns of luxury and excess that can lead to over-indulgence and dissatisfaction. This card reminds you that you can have too much even of a good thing, and joy can quietly turn into boredom.

title: Five of Cups
description: The Five of Cups speaks of parting, pain, sorrow, and disappointment that still have to be lived through. This card reminds you that grief is not a dead end but a stage, and a way out will always be found, as long as you don't stay stuck in it forever.

title: Six of Cups
description: The Six of Cups is joy, sensual desire, and warm memories of the past — a romantic, nostalgic love. This card invites you to feel again the lightness and pleasure your heart has already known once before.

title: Seven of Cups
description: The Seven of Cups warns of illusion and self-deception about your own abilities — it is easy to mistake the false for the real, and disappointment usually follows. This card calls you to see clearly which of the possibilities opening up in front of you is genuinely real.

title: Eight of Cups
description: The Eight of Cups speaks of defeat and loss, but also of a parting that opens the chance to reorient yourself. This card also warns against laziness — sometimes the only way forward is to honestly let go of what no longer works.

title: Nine of Cups
description: The Nine of Cups grants freedom from worry, pleasure, and a genuine joy of life. This is a card of sociability and a spirit of togetherness — a moment when you can relax and simply enjoy what already is.

title: Ten of Cups
description: The Ten of Cups is complete satisfaction, harmony, accord, and love. This card speaks of success in family life, of contentment and deep mutual understanding — a state where the cup of happiness is filled to the brim.

title: Princess of Cups
description: The Princess of Cups is feeling, sensitivity, and a delicate intuition. She carries an emotional freedom, grace, and gentleness, along with the ability to understand others with her heart before her mind catches up.

title: Prince of Cups
description: The Prince of Cups is full of impossible dreams and strong, almost physical longings born from wistful, romantic thoughts. He carries the potential for a deep transformation through sensitivity and ecstatic, almost visionary experiences.

title: Queen of Cups
description: The Queen of Cups is receptivity itself: a mature woman, mother, companion, and beloved, who has access to the most primal wellsprings of knowledge. In her, a nurturing, protective, and comforting nature all come together.

title: Knight of Cups
description: The Knight of Cups is a good and loving father, an attentive and caring partner. A sensitive and sensual man, in whom the soul of an artist and the care of a healer are joined.

title: Ace of Swords
description: The Ace of Swords is a new chance, clear decisions, and liberating thoughts that cut through the fog of doubt. This card opens a new path, one that begins the moment the mind finally finds clarity.

title: Two of Swords
description: The Two of Swords is a truce after conflict, a fragile but real balance settling in after a tense standoff. This card speaks of a temporary but necessary respite between two opposing sides.

title: Three of Swords
description: The Three of Swords speaks of misfortune in love, sorrow, and illness, of doubt and a lack of clarity. This heavy card does not hide the pain, but reminds you that relief usually follows once clarity arrives.

title: Four of Swords
description: The Four of Swords is an imposed silence, an enforced respite, a calm after the storm. This card asks you to accept the pause as a necessity, not as time wasted.

title: Five of Swords
description: The Five of Swords warns of defeat, loss, humiliation, and a dangerous situation. This card demands particular caution and an honest assessment of what's happening before you take your next step.

title: Six of Swords
description: The Six of Swords opens new horizons — a scientific, analytical mind leads to success where emotion would only lead to a dead end. This card is about a clear, sober outlook that carries you forward.

title: Seven of Swords
description: The Seven of Swords speaks of a failing spirit and the futility of your efforts, of obstacles that are largely invented by your own mind. But hidden within this very trial is the chance to emerge from difficulty older and wiser.

title: Eight of Swords
description: The Eight of Swords is indecision and hesitation, a choice between two possibilities that is hard to make. This card is about overcoming an inner obstacle that holds you tighter than any outward circumstance could.

title: Nine of Swords
description: The Nine of Swords speaks of fanaticism and self-torment, of cruelty toward yourself, nightmares, and self-condemnation. This heavy card calls on you to finally stop being your own harshest judge.

title: Ten of Swords
description: The Ten of Swords is an image of violence, an ending, ruin and collapse, of negative thoughts and the fear of losing your mind. But rock bottom is also, at the same time, the one point from which the only way left is up.

title: Princess of Swords
description: The Princess of Swords is a young, airy energy and a will to win, whose speech lands like a weapon. She carries a sharp, almost aggressive edge and an inner rebelliousness that tolerates no obstacle in its way.

title: Prince of Swords
description: The Prince of Swords is a son of the air whose weapon is argument. He leaps easily from one thesis to the next, combining a certain carelessness and skepticism with a freedom from convention, a creative and deeply intuitive mind.

title: Queen of Swords
description: The Queen of Swords is a rational, intellectual, and perceptive woman: sharp-minded, commanding, and hard to reach. She carries a detachment and an emotional coolness — the ability to drop every mask and every role and see things exactly as they are.

title: Knight of Swords
description: The Knight of Swords is abstract, constructive thinking paired with sharp criticism. In him, a keen intellect and ambition combine with the ability to birth genuinely revolutionary thoughts and new syntheses of ideas.

title: Ace of Disks
description: The Ace of Disks is inner and outer wealth, the happiest card in the Minor Arcana. It promises success and recognition, the chance to stand at the summit, having reached what you set out for.

title: Two of Disks
description: The Two of Disks is adaptability, a readiness for change and transformation. This card teaches you to keep your balance at the very moment circumstances demand flexibility and the skill of juggling several tasks at once.

title: Three of Disks
description: The Three of Disks is success that arrives after passing a test: the ability to finish what you started and become genuinely skilled at your craft. This card is about success earned through diligence and hard work, not luck.

title: Four of Disks
description: The Four of Disks speaks of material power and an exaggerated need for security. This card warns against clinging to existing beliefs and an excessive urge to hold on to what you already have instead of moving forward.

title: Five of Disks
description: The Five of Disks points to a crisis and anxiety coming from the outside — an economic problem pressing on your usual stability. This card demands a sober recognition of the difficulty, so a way out can be found.

title: Six of Disks
description: The Six of Disks is reward and success: a project met with genuine support. This card says that you share your success with others, and it comes back to you as shared, collective prosperity.

title: Seven of Disks
description: The Seven of Disks warns: inaction must be overcome. This card says that quick, decisive action is the right path forward, and hesitation will only deepen the stagnation.

title: Eight of Disks
description: The Eight of Disks is the flowering of inner and outer wealth, the moment when diligent work finally bears fruit. This card is about the freedom and creativity that are born from confident mastery.

title: Nine of Disks
description: The Nine of Disks is a fortunate card of profit, harmony, and a genuine enjoyment of the fruits of your labor. It speaks of a moment when you can calmly savor the abundance you have earned.

title: Ten of Disks
description: The Ten of Disks is a rich reward, wealth, and abundance crowning a long road. This card speaks of clear, sound thinking and of a success made manifest on both the material and the immaterial plane.

title: Princess of Disks
description: The Princess of Disks is motherhood, love, and warmth of heart. She carries rebirth and a new beginning, and with it abundance and increase, like earth ready to give a new harvest.

title: Prince of Disks
description: The Prince of Disks is construction and its practical fruits: he is architect and artist at once. In him live the energy, drive, and persistence needed to carry a plan through into reality.

title: Queen of Disks
description: The Queen of Disks is a mature, cheerful, and abundant aspect of femininity: everything lies in her hands, and she manages it exactly as she sees fit. She is a woman deeply attached to material things, with a gift for creating real prosperity around herself.

title: Knight of Disks
description: The Knight of Disks is the patriarch, whose goal is mastery over his own world. Steadfastness, will, and good sense drive him toward an uncompromising pursuit of his own interests, and he turns to spiritual matters only after he has reached his material goal.
